issues.description: Method: orderMeal(Meal). The problem statement UML (problem_statement.md) declares orderMeal(Meal): void, indicating the method should not return a value. The reference implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java) declares public boolean orderMeal(Meal meal) and returns a boolean. This divergence in the declared return type and contract (void vs boolean) can confuse students about the expected signature and behavior, and may cause tests or grading expectations to disagree with the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent. Either (A) change the reference implementation to match the specification by declaring public void orderMeal(Meal meal) and remove the boolean return value (adjust any return sites and tests accordingly), or (B) update the problem statement and UML to declare orderMeal(Meal): boolean and document the meaning of the boolean return (e.g., whether it indicates success). Prefer option A (modify the solution to void) to align with the UML and textual specification unless there is a pedagogical reason to expose a boolean result.
